It\\n then attaches the original root volume to the helper\\n instance.\\n* The system uses Run Command to run EC2Rescue on the helper instance.\\n On Windows, EC2Rescue enables password generation for the local\\n Administrator by using EC2Config or EC2Launch on the attached,\\n original root volume. On Linux, EC2Rescue generates and injects a\\n new SSH key and saves the private key, encrypted, in Parameter Store. When\\n finished, EC2Rescue reattaches the root volume back to the original\\n instance.\\n* The system creates a new Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of your instance, now\\n that password generation is enabled. You can use this AMI to\\n create a new EC2 instance, and associate a new key pair if\\n needed.\\n* The system restarts your original instance, and terminates the\\n temporary instance. The system also terminates the temporary VPC and\\n deletes the EC2Rescue CloudFormation stack created at the start of the\\n automation.\\n* **Windows**: Your instance generates\\n a new password you can decode from the Amazon EC2 console using the\\n current key pair assigned to the instance.\\n\\n **Linux**: You can SSH to the\\n instance by using the SSH key stored in Systems Manager Parameter Store as\\n **/ec2rl/openssh/`instance\\n ID`/key**\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-ec2reset.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Running Verify Aws Claim"}

{"id": "f5c7ca55-be02-4ab1-81bc-213ed4e6dea5", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_zvJpoFX2hNbdXHgpZExQqI", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"AWSSupport-ExecuteEC2Rescue\",\"context\":\"# `AWSSupport-ExecuteEC2Rescue`\\n\\n**Description**\\n\\nThis runbook uses the EC2Rescue tool to troubleshoot and, where possible,\\nrepair common connectivity issues with the specified Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance for Linux or\\nWindows Server. If no role is specified, Systems Manager Automation uses the permissions of\\n the user that starts this runbook.\\n* EC2RescueInstanceType\\n\\n Type: String\\n\\n Valid values: t2.small | t2.medium | t2.large\\n\\n Default: t2.small\\n\\n Description: (Required) The EC2 instance type for the EC2Rescue\\n instance. Make sure the bucket policy does not grant unnecessary\\n read/write permissions to parties that do not need access to the collected\\n logs.\\n* SubnetId\\n\\n Type: String\\n\\n Default: CreateNewVPC\\n\\n Description: (Optional) The subnet ID for the EC2Rescue instance.\\n By default, AWS Systems Manager Automation creates a new VPC. Alternatively, use\\n `SelectedInstanceSubnet` to use the same subnet as your instance, or\\n specify a custom subnet ID.\\n\\n **Important:**\\n\\n The subnet must be in the same Availability Zone as\\n `UnreachableInstanceId`, and it must allow access to the SSM\\n endpoints.\\n* UnreachableInstanceId\\n\\n Type: String\\n\\n Description: (Required) ID of your unreachable EC2 instance.\\n\\n **Important:**\\n\\n Systems Manager Automation stops this instance, and creates an AMI before attempting any\\n operations. Data stored in instance store volumes will be lost. The public IP\\n address will change if you are not using an Elastic IP address.\\n\\n**Required IAM permissions**\\n\\nThe `AutomationAssumeRole`\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager-automation-runbooks/latest/userguide/automation-awssupport-executeec2rescue.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Run the EC2Rescue tool on unreachable instances\",\"context\":\"# Run the EC2Rescue tool on unreachable instances\\n\\nEC2Rescue can help you diagnose and troubleshoot problems on Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)\\ninstances for Linux and Windows Server. Or, you can run the tool automatically\\nby using Systems Manager Automation and the **`AWSSupport-ExecuteEC2Rescue`** runbook. Automation\\nis a tool in AWS Systems Manager. For more information, see Run the EC2Rescue tool on\\nunreachable instances.\\n\\nThe AWSSupport-ExecuteEC2Rescue automation document requires a stop and\\nrestart of the instance. Systems Manager Automation stops the instance and creates an\\nAmazon Machine Image (AMI). Data stored in instance store volumes is lost.\\nThe public IP address changes if you are not using an Elastic IP address.\\nFor more information, see Run the EC2Rescue tool on\\nunreachable instances in the\\n*AWS Systems Manager User Guide*.\\n\\n###### To troubleshoot using the AWSSupport-ExecuteEC2Rescue document\\n\\n1. Open the Systems Manager\\n console.\\n2. Verify that you are in the same Region as the impaired Amazon EC2\\n instance.\\n3. In the navigation panel, choose **Documents**.\\n4. Search for and select the `AWSSupport-ExecuteEC2Rescue` document,\\n and then choose **Execute automation**.\\n5. In **Execution Mode**, choose **Simple execution**.\\n6. In the **Input parameters** section, for\\n **UnreachableInstanceId**, enter the\\n Amazon EC2 instance ID of the unreachable instance.\\n7. (Optional) For **LogDestination**, enter the Amazon Simple Storage Service\\n (Amazon S3) bucket name if you want to collect operating system logs for\\n troubleshooting your Amazon EC2 instance. Logs are automatically uploaded to the\\n specified bucket.\\n8. Choose **Execute**.\\n9. To monitor the execution progress, in **Execution\\n status**, wait for the status to change from **Pending** to **Success**. Expand **Outputs**\\n to view the results. A pending reboot normally indicates that updates are pending, and a reboot\\n is required before performing additional updates.\\n* Configures the proxy settings at the operating system level, which can help\\n troubleshoot connectivity issues.\\n* Performs an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) endpoint connectivity test and calls the `GetDeployablePatchSnapshotForInstance` API operation to\\n retrieve the current snapshot for the patch baseline the managed node uses.\\n* If the connection fails, provides the option to run the\\n `AWSSupport-AnalyzeAWSEndpointReachabilityFromEC2` runbook to analyze\\n the instance's connectivity to Amazon S3 endpoints.\\n* Validates the Windows updates configuration and tests Windows Server Update\\n Services (WSUS) (if applicable).\\n\\n**Important:**\\n\\n* Active Directory domain controllers are not supported.\\n* Windows Server version 2008 R2 or previous versions are not supported.\\n* SSM Agent 1.2.371 or previous versions are not supported.\\n* The `AWSSupport-AnalyzeAWSEndpointReachabilityFromEC2` runbook uses\\n `VPC\\n Reachability Analyzer` to analyze the network connectivity\\n between a source and a service endpoint. Covers Python (pymssql, pyodbc), .NET (Microsoft.Data.SqlClient), Java (JDBC mssql-jdbc), Node.js (tedious), IAM auth via RDS Proxy, and VPC/ECS/EKS/Lambda deployment.\\n\\nServices: rds, secretsmanager, ec2, lambda, ecs, eks, directoryservice\\nTasks: connect, configure, troubleshoot, deploy, authenticate, create, provision, modify\\nPersona: developer, devops, dba\\nWorkload: application, legacy-migration, .net, java, python, nodejs\\n*\",\"skill_name\":\"rds-sqlserver\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Running Verify Aws Claim"}

## Runbooks to use

**1. `AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH`** is the first one to try.
- It installs EC2Rescue for Linux and checks for, or fixes, common issues that block SSH. It also works on instances that aren't managed by Systems Manager.
- `Action` is `CheckAll` (the default, read-only) or `FixAll` (check and fix).
- `AllowOffline` is `false` by default. If you set it to `true`, the runbook can stop the instance and create an AMI before it remediates offline.
- `InstanceId` is required.
- Start with `CheckAll`. Move to `FixAll` only once you've seen what it finds.

**2. `AWSSupport-ExecuteEC2Rescue`** is the heavier fallback.
- It troubleshoots and repairs connectivity problems by attaching the root volume to a helper instance.
- It stops your instance and creates an AMI.
- Instance-store data is lost.
- The public IP changes unless you use an Elastic IP.
- Encrypted root volumes aren't supported.

**3. `AWSSupport-ResetAccess`** applies if the cause is a lost or wrong key pair.
- On Linux it generates a new SSH key and stores it in Parameter Store under `/ec2rl/openssh/<instance-id>/key`.
- It stops and restarts the instance.

## Check the network first

SSH timing out, as opposed to "connection refused" or "permission denied", usually means packets aren't reaching sshd. These are the likely causes, and the runbooks above may not fix them:
- The security group doesn't allow inbound TCP 22 from your current source IP. Your IP may have changed.
- A network ACL blocks port 22 or the ephemeral return ports.
- The route table has no route to an internet gateway, or the instance has lost its public IP.
- The instance is failing its status checks or is overloaded.

VPC Reachability Analyzer can show which hop blocks the path. If the instance is a Systems Manager managed node, Session Manager lets you get in without SSH. The EC2 Serial Console is another way in on supported instance types.

I can run read-only checks on the instance in us-east-1. These would cover its security groups, NACLs, route table, public IP, status checks and SSM status. If you give me the instance ID, I'll look. Starting a runbook is a change that needs your approval, so I'd ask before running one.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
